sections.heading: Priors disclosure
sections.markdown: AUTO is read as a low-growth autoparts cyclical whose profit is propped up by associate income, so the market pays it a low multiple and treats the earnings mix as low quality.

sections.heading: Bottom-up estimates
sections.detail: committed first — timestamp above, before any market number
sections.markdown:
FY2024A/FY2025A from the dossier; estimates mine, IDR bn or per share.

| | FY2024A | FY2025A | FY2026E | FY2027E | FY2028E |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | 19,073.7 | 19,906.8 | 22,700 | 24,510 | 26,230 |
| EBIT | 1,081.0 | 1,265.9 | 1,350 | 1,507 | 1,639 |
| Net income | 2,033.6 | 2,205.0 | 2,464 | 2,664 | 2,842 |
| EPS (IDR) | 422.0 | 457.5 | 511 | 553 | 590 |
| DPS (IDR) | 192.0 | 242.5 | 256 | 276 | 295 |

**Driver basis.** 9M-2026 revenue Rp17,021.9bn, +15.0% (dossier quarterly table). Q4 at 5,678 (+11.3%) gives FY2026E 22,700; then +8%/+7% — no growth above the 2026 run-rate. 9M EBIT 999.0 = 5.87% vs 6.36% FY2025, so FY2026E EBIT 1,350 (5.95%), recovering only to 6.25% by FY2028 — below FY2025. Non-operating net (EBIT-to-PBT bridge) was 1,231–1,259 in FY2024/25 and ~1,040 in 9M-2026: I carry it flat-to-modest, not at the +42% jump the house model assumes. Tax 12% is the FY2025 blended effective rate (F34/F33 = 11.05%), low because associate income arrives already taxed.

sections.heading: EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS gate
sections.markdown:
- **Accruals:** (NI − CFO)/avg assets = 1.2% FY2025, 2.4% FY2024, 0.0% FY2023 (CFO = dossier FCF + capex). Clean.
- **Divergence:** FY2025 NI 2,205.0 vs EBIT 1,265.9 — **45% of PBT is non-operating**, of which Rp1,176.9bn is associate/JV equity income (F9). Optics-class, disclosed, tax-exempt at investee. Haircut, not auto-pass.
- **Data defect:** the dossier EBITDA row (2,847.8) is not EBIT + D&A (1,265.9 + 587.2 = 1,853.1); the gap is the non-operating line. Use EBIT and D&A 587.2 (2.95% of revenue, confirmed in the notes as F4). House model uses 1,853.2.
- **IDX regime:** no *papan pemantauan khusus* status and no notation letter in the dossier; shares constant 4,819.7m for four years — no dilution or rights pattern. Not fully clearable from the pack.
- **Related-party:** 34.76% of revenue (F12), structural to the Astra ecosystem, disclosed. Governance discount, not manipulation.
- **Structure flags:** none found — checked (no revaluation, no pledged-stake disclosure, no auditor note).

sections.heading: Variant perception
sections.markdown:
**Market believes:** AUTO is a controlled, 20%-float autoparts supplier whose earnings are half non-operating and geared to a weakening car cycle, so it deserves a discount and little analyst attention.
**Why wrong:** at Rp3,220 net cash (4,527) plus associate/JV stakes at book (7,451) plus investment properties cover 74% of the market cap — the operating business is valued at ~3.1x trailing EV/EBIT, and 2.0x at my 3,000 entry. The Rp1,176.9bn associate line is recurring Denso/GS Battery/Akabono/Kayaba income that arrives tax-paid (the 11.05% blended rate is the tell, not a red flag), and 9M revenue +15% with manufacturing-led volume contradicts decay.
**What proves us wrong:** associate income below Rp900bn, or EBIT margin under 5.5% with revenue stalls — then the discount is about the business, not the structure.

sections.heading: Disconfirming facts
sections.markdown:
1. Margin is compressing, not recovering: 9M-2026 EBIT margin 5.87% vs 6.36% FY2025, and the faster-growing manufacturing segment carries the lower gross margin (dossier quarterly table; house report §1).
2. The "de-rated" premise is partly spent: +52.6% over 12 months, 4.7% off the 52-week high (screen row, 2026-11-07).
3. 34.76% of revenue is related-party (F12) under an 80.0% shareholder (F26); minorities have no mechanism to force the discount shut.
4. 45% of pre-tax profit is associate income the parent does not operationally control (F9 1,176.9 vs F33 2,639.5).
5. A 20% float means index and flow mechanics, not fundamentals, can set the price for years.

sections.heading: Pre-mortem
sections.markdown: It is Q4-2029 and we lost 30%. The discount never closed: Astra allocated at group level, the Japanese JV partners repriced or EV content loss hit the associate line, and a 20% float never produced a bid to mark the operating business above 2x. Worse, the kill filled badly — one 25% ARB band puts 2,375 at 1,781, −41% from a 3,000 entry, because .JK names can ARB-lock for sessions.

sections.heading: IDX microstructure
sections.markdown: Astra International holds 80.0% (F26); free float 20%, no pledged-stake or rights history. 30d ADV Rp8.78bn (the liquidity feed) vs a Rp15bn book: a 5% position is 0.43 days at 20% participation — no liquidity constraint, no discount. Price 3,220 sits in the 25% ARA/ARB band (>Rp200–5,000): daily floor 2,415, ceiling 4,025; board lot 100 = Rp322,000. Flows stale (`fund record` = `{}`), so no flow narrative is underwritten.

sections.heading: Macro stance
sections.markdown: **AGAINST.** The 2026-11-07 memo holds INDO rate-sensitive and consumer-discretionary at AVOID on funding-leg pressure, and autoparts is consumer-discretionary; the Rp4.5tn net cash insulates the discount-rate channel but not imported component costs or purchasing power at USD/IDR 18,003.

sections.heading: Valuation, EV math and edge
sections.markdown:
**Phase-1 correction, disclosed:** the committed valuation used a blanket 0.65×NI FCFE conversion, which wrongly haircut *operating* cash flow (capex 2.7% vs D&A 2.95% means operating FCF converts near 100%). Operating lines are unchanged; the valuation was rebuilt on operating FCFF plus the same book bridge the house uses. It lands at 4,867 against the house's independent 4,875 — the corroboration is the reason I accept the correction.

Target 4,810 = blend above. Kill 2,375 = asset floor. Entry 3,000 = 0.62× base, 5.4x FY2027E EPS, 0.85x forward book, and 1.5x EV/EBIT on the operating business. up 60.3% / down −20.8%, p 0.40 / 0.60, carry 8.28%/yr net × 3y on the up leg only, drag 1.5% → **expected +20.1%/3y (6.3%/yr)**. Win state 83.6%/3y = 22.5%/yr, clearing the FR+4% ≈ 11.2% hurdle; the probability-weighted 6.3%/yr does not, and that gap is the honest cost of the 0.40 prior.

`up/|down|` 3.75 vs the archetype library 1.67 — above, not below: the kill is the asset floor, not a stop. Own-Kelly **+93** vs library-Kelly **+13.3**; the whole gap is (a) down −20.8 vs −30, bought by the cash-plus-stakes floor, and (b) up 60.3 vs 50, bought by an entry 38% under base value. ARB-adjusted (one band below the kill) downside is −41%, at which own-Kelly falls to ~0 — the edge is thin if the kill gaps, which is why size belongs at the low end.

sections.heading: House coverage reconciliation
sections.markdown: My base 4,810 sits between the house's blended 4,488 and its 4,837 target; our DCFs agree to 0.2% (4,867 vs 4,875) because we share the bridge — associates and JVs at book, net cash added, minority deducted, investment properties at carrying value. Two real differences. First, my P/E leg is struck on FY2027E EPS 553 rather than trailing, which lifts it. Second, my bear is 2,375, the asset floor with the operating business valued at zero, against the house's shock-built 3,967 — their bear still prices the opco at ~2.5x EV/EBIT. On a 20% float with a contested structural discount, I do not think that is a bear case; it is the base case with a different label.

The house's reverse DCF (coverage_doc §4) has 3,220 already implying −14.8% FY2027E revenue growth for a decade; at 2,000 the market prices worse, with no catalyst to reverse it.
